result:
I changed `build_invoice` in `meterbill/invoices/builder.py` to look up each country's tax rate once per invoice. Before, `TaxResolver.rate_for` re-read and re-parsed `tax_rates.json` and `tax_overrides.json` for every invoice line. The 376 existing tests pass. I did not time it, because the repo has no October events data to run the invoice against.

The tenant and issue date are fixed within one invoice, so the cached rate is always the one the old code would have computed. Rounding, line taxes and error behaviour are unchanged. A missing or invalid rate still raises the same `TaxError` on the first line that needs it.

I left `TaxResolver` alone. It still reads the files on every call, as its docstring says, and `quote.py` still calls it directly. Putting the cache inside the resolver would also speed up quotes. It would mean tax-file edits are no longer picked up by a long-lived resolver, so I didn't make that change.

The remaining cost is one file read per distinct country per invoice. If a full run is still slow, the next place to look is the per-tenant invoice loop. I can profile that if you can point me at the October data.
